witness_description: No genuine witness. Under the standard tree-exchange reading (e1 constrained to lie on the unique cycle of T + e2), no violation exists anywhere in the swept space. Only a strawman unconstrained reading (arbitrary e1 in T, arbitrary e2 not in T) fails, e.g. n=4, G = {(0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(1,2)}, T = {(0,1),(0,2),(0,3)}, e1 = (0,3), e2 = (1,2): T' = {(0,1),(0,2),(1,2)} is disconnected (vertex 3 isolated), hence not a spanning tree - but that reading is not clearly what the fragment asserts.
refutation_explanation: The quoted claim is a sentence fragment: 'spanning tree T' by removing e1 from T and adding the other edge e2.' It never defines the graph, how e1 is chosen, or the antecedent of 'the other edge e2', so the relation between e1 and e2 is not supplied by the claim text. Under the standard exchange-lemma reading (e2 a non-tree edge, e1 on the unique cycle of T + e2) the claim is a theorem and the exhaustive sweep found no counterexample. Under the unconstrained reading it is trivially false (witness above), but refuting that reading refutes only an interpretation the text does not clearly assert. Since the claim text under-determines which reading is meant, no counterexample to the claim as written can be honestly certified.
search_space: All connected labeled simple graphs on n in {3,4,5} vertices (every edge subset of the complete graph, connectivity-filtered: 770 graphs), all spanning trees of each (8134 trees), and for each tree all pairs (e1 in T, e2 in E(G)\T): 96582 unconstrained pairs (Reading A) of which 59958 satisfy the cycle constraint e1 in cycle(T+e2) (Reading B). Deterministic lexicographic enumeration, exact integer union-find arithmetic, no floats, no randomness.
